title: Neighbouring courses must really differ
statement: A course for one level must differ from the course for the level beside it in more than its lesson list, difficulty and units, because near-copies share their weaknesses.
detail: The course-plan agents made a sibling clone a blocking finding: a design whose only differences from the nearest sibling are lesson spines, difficulty and units fails review (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/course-formula-agents.md`, lines 99-101). Every design first loads a grade-band profile of the dimensions that must differ by grade, among them text band, stamina, genre split, item formats, depth-of-knowledge mix and gate design (the same file, lines 89-91). The rule answered a standing concern that courses for neighbouring grades built under the same guidance were so alike that one rejection would bring the rest for the same underlying reasons (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/grade-band-profiles.md`).
against: The joint rejection is a stated concern, not an observed outcome.

evidence.quote: **"Sibling clone" is a blocking red-team finding class**: a design whose only deltas from the nearest sibling are lesson spines/difficulty/units fails review
dimensions that MUST differ by grade (axis, decoding share, text band, stamina, schema progression, genre split, item formats, DOK mix, gate design, anchor)
